# layout

```go
import "github.com/lucasassuncao/bezel/layout"
```

Package layout declares a screen as a tree of named leaves and resolves it to rectangles. It knows nothing about what is drawn in them.

<a name="ClampScroll"></a>
## func [ClampScroll](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/bezel/blob/main/layout/scroll.go#L6>)

```go
func ClampScroll(cursor, offset, height int) int
```

ClampScroll moves offset so that cursor stays inside a window of height rows: up when the cursor is above it, down when below. Never negative; a non\-positive height only applies the floor.

<a name="Leaves"></a>
## func [Leaves](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/bezel/blob/main/layout/layout.go#L98>)

```go
func Leaves(n Node) iter.Seq[Leaf]
```

Leaves yields every leaf under n, depth\-first in declaration order.

<a name="Resolve"></a>
## func [Resolve](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/bezel/blob/main/layout/resolve.go#L6>)

```go
func Resolve(n Node, body Rect, present func(name string) bool) (map[string]Rect, bool)
```

Resolve places the tree inside body. Leaves that present rejects are pruned first, so their space goes to their siblings. collapsed reports whether any Collapse fired, which is what a legend needs to change its wording.

<a name="ScrollStart"></a>
## func [ScrollStart](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/bezel/blob/main/layout/scroll.go#L18>)

```go
func ScrollStart(cursor, total, height int) int
```

ScrollStart keeps the cursor inside a window of height rows without jumping around: centred on it where the list allows.

<a name="Scroll"></a>
## type [Scroll](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/bezel/blob/main/layout/scroll.go#L89>)

Scroll is how much of Total rows a window shows, from Offset: what a scrollbar draws. The zero value draws none.

```go
type Scroll struct{ Offset, Visible, Total int }
```

<a name="Scroll.Thumb"></a>
### func \(Scroll\) [Thumb](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/bezel/blob/main/layout/scroll.go#L101>)

```go
func (s Scroll) Thumb(track int) (pos, size int)
```

Thumb places a scrollbar's thumb on a track rows long: from pos, size rows, and size 0 when every row shows. The thumb touches an end of the track only while the window does, so it never reads as the top when it is not.

<a name="Window"></a>
## type [Window](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/bezel/blob/main/layout/scroll.go#L28>)

Window is the part of a list that fits in Height rows, from Offset, kept on Cursor. While rows overflow below it, its last row says how many more there are instead of showing one, the way list and tree draw "↓ N more".

```go
type Window struct{ Cursor, Offset, Height int }
```

<a name="Window.Bounds"></a>
### func \(Window\) [Bounds](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/bezel/blob/main/layout/scroll.go#L70>)

```go
func (w Window) Bounds(n int) (start, end, below int)
```

Bounds is the rows \[start, end\) of n that w shows, and the count its "more" row reports, zero when it has none. Clamp w first.

<a name="Window.Clamp"></a>
### func \(Window\) [Clamp](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/bezel/blob/main/layout/scroll.go#L32>)

```go
func (w Window) Clamp(n int) Window
```

Clamp fits w to n rows: the cursor on one of them, no blank rows under a list scrolled past its end, and the cursor clear of the "more" row.

<a name="Window.Move"></a>
### func \(Window\) [Move](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/bezel/blob/main/layout/scroll.go#L46>)

```go
func (w Window) Move(delta, n int, skip func(i int) bool) Window
```

Move steps the cursor delta rows of n, passing over the ones skip reports \(nil skips none\) and stopping at the last row it can land on.

<a name="Window.Scroll"></a>
### func \(Window\) [Scroll](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/bezel/blob/main/layout/scroll.go#L93>)

```go
func (w Window) Scroll(n int) Scroll
```

Scroll is w over n rows, as a scrollbar sees it: the "more" row is not one of the rows shown. Clamp w first.
